engine_notes: BrowserQuest is a 2D HTML5 Canvas and WebSocket/offline-capable action-RPG that loads all visual assets at three integer pixel scales (1x in client/img/1/, 2x in client/img/2/, and 3x in client/img/3/) relative to a base 16x16 pixel tile grid. Sprite sheet metadata lives in individual JSON files under client/sprites/*.json (bundled via RequireJS text! in client/js/sprites.js), specifying base 1x frame width, height, offset_x/offset_y anchor relative to the 16x16 tile top-left, and named animation rows; left-facing animations are generated at runtime by horizontally flipping the *_right rows across the 16px tile width. The player character is rendered by compositing the currently equipped armor sprite sheet (starting with clotharmor) underneath the equipped weapon sprite sheet (starting with sword1) using matching animation row and frame indices, while hurt flashes (red/pink RGB tint) and hover silhouettes (1px yellow-white outline) are generated procedurally on offscreen canvases in client/js/sprite.js. Terrain is drawn from client/img/{1,2,3}/tilesheet.png using map definitions in client/maps/world_client.json (and client/maps/world_client.js for the web worker), which specify ground/high layers, animated tile sequences, collision/plateau grids, door teleports, and music areas. World entity placement (player spawn checkpoints, static NPCs, static mobs, roaming mob areas, static chests, and chest reward areas) is loaded by the server (server/maps/world_server.json) or offline client (client/maps/world_server.json). NPC dialogue is defined as sequential string arrays per NPC kind in NpcTalk inside client/js/npc.js, while quests are implemented as 20 achievements in client/js/game.js triggered by map zones, kill counters, damage taken, NPC talks, and item looting. UI chrome, HUD bars, achievement badges, fonts (GraphicPixel and AdvoCut), and colours are styled via client/css/main.css and client/css/achievements.css using multi-resolution sprite atlases (spritesheet.png, barsheet.png, achievements.png) alongside canvas text/cell colours in client/js/renderer.js and client/js/infomanager.js.
